T: This menu will self-destruct in five seconds.
D: An agent framed for his team's deaths goes rogue to find the real mole.
P: Serve the mains when Ethan meets Kittridge at the restaurant with the giant fish tanks.
S: Baguette slices topped with potato salad, ham and sliced egg

Little Czech open sandwiches on buttered baguette, piled with potato salad, ham, boiled egg, gherkin and parsley, the way Prague delis line them up. Boil 3 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and slice. Slice a baguette into 16 pieces and spread with butter. Top each with a spoon of potato salad, a fold of ham, a slice of boiled egg, a gherkin slice and parsley. Line them up neatly on a long board.
Fresh fried prawn crackers served with sweet chili and lime sauce
Prawn crackers fried at 190C for a few seconds until they puff up dramatically, served with a sweet chilli and lime dip.
the white vault at Langley he drops into on a wire

An all-white board of brie, goat's cheese and whipped ricotta stacked on white water crackers with crisp pear, white pepper and a little honey. Beat 150g ricotta with a pinch of salt until smooth. Slice 150g brie and 120g goat's cheese into neat pieces. Core and thinly slice 2 pears and toss in lemon juice. Stack crackers with a layer of cheese, a slice of pear and a crack of white pepper, and drizzle a little honey over. Lay out on a white plate and serve in silence.
M: Beef braised 3 hours with onions, sweet paprika and caraway
Beef chuck browned, plenty of onion cooked down slowly, sweet paprika, caraway and tomato, braised at 160C for 3 hours. Bread dumplings or crusty bread.
the restaurant with the giant fish tanks, before they burst

Snapper fillets pan-fried skin down until crackling, finished with nutty brown butter, capers and lemon, with crushed dill potatoes. Boil 800g small potatoes for 15 minutes, drain and crush with 30g butter, chopped dill and salt. Score the skin of 4 snapper fillets, season and fry skin side down in 2 tbsp oil for 4 minutes until crisp, then flip for 1 minute. Remove the fish, add 60g butter to the pan and cook until nut brown, then add 1 tbsp capers and the juice of a lemon. Spoon over the fish.
W: Sweet yeast dough baked around rolling pins, rolled in cinnamon sugar and walnuts
Sweet yeasted dough wrapped around foil-covered rolling pins, rolled in cinnamon sugar and walnuts, baked at 200C for 15 minutes until golden, slid off and filled with whipped cream.
K: Pilsner and ginger syrup in a smoked salt rimmed glass

Cold Czech pilsner topped with fresh lemon, ginger syrup and soda in a smoked salt rimmed glass, with a crackle of lemon zest. Simmer 50g sugar, 50ml water and a sliced 3cm piece of ginger for 5 minutes and cool. Rub the rims of four glasses with lemon and dip in smoked salt. Add 20ml ginger syrup and the juice of half a lemon to each glass, pour in 330ml cold Czech pilsner and top with a splash of soda water. Finish with grated lemon zest.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool and slice.
Slice the baguette into rounds and spread with butter.
Top each with potato salad, a fold of ham, a slice of egg, a gherkin slice and parsley.
Line them up neatly on a long board.
Fry a few crackers at a time for a few seconds until they puff up dramatically. Drain on paper towel.
Mix the sweet chilli sauce with the lime juice and serve for dipping.

dishes.make_ahead: Better the next day, keeps 3 days chilled

steps.text: Brown the beef in batches in a hot heavy pot.
Cook the onions slowly for 20 minutes, then stir in the paprika, caraway and tomato paste.
Add the water, return the beef and cover. Braise at 160C for 3 hours.
Season and serve with crusty bread.

dishes.make_ahead: Best eaten the day it is baked

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, a little of the sugar, milk, butter and egg into a soft dough and knead.
Roll out, cut into strips and wrap around foil-covered rolling pins. Roll in cinnamon, the rest of the sugar and the walnuts.
Slide off the pins and fill with whipped cream.

dishes.make_ahead: Syrup up to 1 week ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Simmer the sugar, water and ginger for 5 minutes, then cool and strain.
Rub the rims of four glasses with lemon and dip in smoked salt.
Add some ginger syrup and the juice of half a lemon to each glass. Pour in the pilsner, top with soda water and finish with grated lemon zest.

s.note: Fresh fried prawn crackers served with sweet chili and lime sauce
s.how: Fry a few prawn crackers at a time at 190C for a few seconds until they puff up dramatically. Drain and serve with sweet chilli sauce mixed with lime juice.

m.note: Beef braised 3 hours with onions, sweet paprika and caraway
m.how: Brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck. Cook 3 sliced onions slowly for 20 minutes, then add 2 tbsp sweet paprika, 1 tsp caraway and 2 tbsp tomato paste. Add 750ml water, return the beef and braise at 160C for 3 hours. Serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Sweet yeast dough baked around rolling pins, rolled in cinnamon sugar and walnuts
w.how: Mix 400g flour, 7g yeast, 50g sugar, 200ml warm milk, 60g butter and 1 egg and prove an hour. Wrap strips around foil-covered rolling pins, roll in cinnamon sugar and chopped walnuts and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Slide off and fill with 300ml whipped cream.

Add 20ml ginger syrup and the juice of half a lemon to each glass, pour in 330ml cold Czech pilsner and top with a splash of soda water. Finish with grated lemon zest.
